plan.subject: Marketing science

queries.query: ("charm pricing" OR "left-digit effect" OR ".99 pricing" OR "9-ending prices") AND (marketing OR consumer OR retail OR pricing OR ecommerce)
queries.rationale: Targets evidence on whether psychological price endings still shift purchase behavior, a core pricing-test question for DTC commerce.

queries.query: ("price promotion" OR "temporary price reduction" OR "sales promotion" OR couponing) AND (marketing OR consumer OR retail OR ecommerce OR brand)
queries.rationale: Catches work on discounts, coupons, and promotional mechanics that affect demand lift beyond generic pricing papers.

queries.query: ("promotion-focused pricing" OR "discount framing" OR "price discount framing" OR "percent-off framing") AND (marketing OR consumer OR retail OR ecommerce OR advertising)
queries.rationale: Focuses on how the presentation of a discount changes response, which is different from whether a discount exists at all.

queries.query: ("price fairness" OR "perceived price unfairness" OR "price image" OR "reference price") AND (marketing OR consumer OR retail OR ecommerce OR brand)
queries.rationale: Finds research on when prices and promos backfire by changing fairness perceptions or consumers' internal price benchmarks.

queries.query: ("brand dilution" OR "promotion-induced brand switching" OR "deal proneness" OR "promotion wearout") AND (marketing OR consumer OR retail OR ecommerce OR brand)
queries.rationale: Targets the downside of repeated promotions, especially brand erosion and weaker loyalty after discount-heavy tactics.

queries.query: ("scarcity appeal" OR "limited-time offer" OR "limited quantity" OR "stock scarcity") AND (marketing OR consumer OR retail OR ecommerce OR checkout)
queries.rationale: Covers the behavioral effects of urgency and low-stock signals on purchase likelihood, especially near checkout.

queries.query: ("social proof" OR "popularity cue" OR "customer review" OR "review valence") AND (marketing OR consumer OR ecommerce OR retail OR conversion)
queries.rationale: Retrieves evidence on how ratings, review signals, and popularity cues change conversion rather than broader reputation theory.

queries.query: ("online review helpfulness" OR "review volume" OR "average rating" OR "review credibility") AND (marketing OR consumer OR ecommerce OR retail OR platform)
queries.rationale: Adds nuance on which review metrics actually move shoppers, complementing broader social-proof work with more operational levers.

queries.query: ("message framing" OR "gain-loss framing" OR "attribute framing" OR "goal framing") AND (marketing OR consumer OR advertising OR persuasion OR ecommerce)
queries.rationale: Surfaces findings on how wording and framing alter response, useful for ad creative and landing-page copy tests.

queries.query: ("advertising creativity" OR "ad creativity" OR "creative advertising" OR "advertising appeal") AND (marketing OR consumer OR advertising OR persuasion OR digital)
queries.rationale: Targets research on which creative characteristics improve ad performance, distinct from pricing or copy-framing studies.

queries.query: ("emotional appeal" OR "informational appeal" OR "rational appeal" OR "transformational advertising") AND (marketing OR consumer OR advertising OR digital OR persuasion)
queries.rationale: Captures evidence comparing creative appeal styles, which is useful when deciding what kind of ad concept is more likely to convert.

queries.query: ("visual attention" OR "eye tracking" OR "visual salience" OR "gaze pattern") AND (marketing OR consumer OR advertising OR package OR ecommerce)
queries.angle: visual attention in creative and pages
queries.rationale: Finds studies on what design elements actually attract attention in ads, packaging, and product pages.

queries.query: ("choice architecture" OR "default option" OR nudging OR "behavioral nudge") AND (marketing OR consumer OR ecommerce OR retail OR "behavioral economics")
queries.rationale: Covers practical behavioral interventions that can move conversion without changing the underlying offer.

queries.query: ("decoy effect" OR "compromise effect" OR "asymmetric dominance" OR "attraction effect") AND (marketing OR consumer OR pricing OR choice OR retail)
queries.rationale: Targets assortment and offer-architecture effects that influence which product or plan shoppers choose.

queries.query: ("product naming" OR "brand name" OR "brand naming" OR "product name fluency") AND (marketing OR consumer OR branding OR retail OR ecommerce)
queries.rationale: Retrieves evidence on how names, fluency, and linguistic features affect perception and purchase response.

queries.query: ("processing fluency" OR "name fluency" OR "linguistic fluency" OR "pronounceability") AND (marketing OR consumer OR branding OR advertising OR product)
queries.rationale: Adds the psychological mechanism behind naming and copy effects, helping explain why some words convert better than others.

queries.query: ("landing page" OR "website conversion" OR "conversion rate optimization" OR "online purchase intention") AND (marketing OR ecommerce OR retail OR digital OR consumer)
queries.rationale: Provides a recall-safety query for website and page-level conversion research that may not use narrower persuasion terminology.

queries.query: ("personalized pricing" OR "price personalization" OR "personalized promotion" OR "targeted promotion") AND (marketing OR consumer OR retail OR ecommerce OR digital)
queries.rationale: Catches work on tailoring prices and promotions, an important applied lever for growth teams beyond one-size-fits-all campaigns.

plan.coverage_notes: This plan emphasizes practical levers a growth marketer can test: pricing, discount framing, promo downside risk, scarcity, reviews, ad creative, framing, product naming, choice architecture, and page conversion. It deliberately skips advertising history, media theory, and broad branding discourse in favor of query shapes likely to surface empirical consumer-response research. I assumed the reader wants evidence that translates into experiments on e-commerce funnels and merchandising decisions, so several queries are tuned to retail, ecommerce, and conversion contexts rather than general communications scholarship.
